stem: A nurse is teaching a client to self-administer enoxaparin from a prefilled syringe. Which client action demonstrates correct technique?

options.A: Expel the air bubble from the prefilled syringe before injecting so no air enters the subcutaneous tissue
options.B: Inject deeply into a skin fold of the abdomen, alternate sites, and avoid rubbing the site after the injection
options.C: Give the medication intramuscularly in the deltoid because muscle absorption is more predictable
options.D: Use the same abdominal site each day to reduce variation in anticoagulant effect

rationale: Current enoxaparin labeling instructs subcutaneous administration into an abdominal skin fold, alternation of injection sites, and no rubbing after injection to reduce bruising. The air bubble in a prefilled syringe should not be expelled because doing so can cause loss of medication. Intramuscular administration is not recommended.
educational_objective: Teach evidence-based enoxaparin prefilled-syringe self-injection technique.
source_locator: Section 2.5 Administration — deep SC injection; do not expel air bubble; alternate abdominal sites; hold skin fold; do not rub after injection
source_claim_supported: Enoxaparin self-injection technique includes deep subcutaneous abdominal administration, site rotation, retention of the prefilled-syringe air bubble and no rubbing afterward.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
